text: Hyperliquid liquidation price formula (docs): liq_price = price - side * margin_available / position_size / (1 - l * side), where l = 1 / MAINTENANCE_LEVERAGE, side = 1 for long and -1 for short, margin_available (cross) = account_value - maintenance_margin_required, and margin_available (isolated) = isolated_margin - maintenance_margin_required. For tiered assets, maintenance leverage comes from the margin tier matching position value at the liquidation price. The cross-margin liquidation price does not depend on the leverage setting; the isolated one does. Displayed estimates can drift with book liquidity, funding payments and unrealized PnL on other cross positions. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

text: Both Drift-lineage codebases socialize a perp residual by dividing it by the market's total open base (absolute long base plus absolute short base), adding the result to the long cumulative funding rate and subtracting it from the short rate. Every open position pays per unit of base, once, whatever its side or profit, and no position is closed. Drift's docs say the same: 'paid for pro-rata (by base amount) by all open positions'. A spot residual instead lowers the deposit interest index, a pro-rata haircut to every lender in that market. (high confidence)

text: Each spot market has its own insurance fund, held in that market's asset. The quote-asset fund backs every perp. Stakers hold shares. To unstake, a staker requests, waits (13 days by default, set per spot market), then withdraws. The payout uses the lower of the share price at request and at withdrawal. A draw after the request therefore reaches the staker and a gain does not. (high confidence)

text: Both codebases socialize the last residual with a cumulative funding-rate bump, not by closing positions. calculate_funding_rate_deltas_to_resolve_bankruptcy divides the residual loss, rounded up, by total open base, which is the absolute long base plus the absolute short base. The program adds that delta to the long cumulative funding rate and subtracts it from the short rate, so longs and shorts both owe the same amount per unit of base, once, at resolution. The call fails with CantResolvePerpBankruptcy if total open base is zero. Velocity's docs give an example: a $2,000,000 residual over 100,000 SOL long and 100,000 SOL short costs $10 per SOL.
